core_obligations: Choose an open submodule with I-adic topology and note that the powers of the ideal times it form a fundamental system of open submodules of the module, so that its completion sits inside the completion of the module as an open submodule (proof lines 1032-1037).
Conclude that this submodule has I-adic topology by the algebra statement on completions with respect to a finitely generated ideal (proof lines 1037-1039).

Choose generators of a power of the ideal, note that the induced map from a finite direct sum onto the ideal times the module is continuous and open, and apply the exactness statement for short exact sequences under completion to obtain a surjection from the completion of the finite direct sum onto the kernel of the map to the quotient (proof lines 1039-1051).
Conclude that the completion modulo the power of the ideal agrees with the module modulo that power (proof lines 1051-1053).
proof_roadmap: The open submodule and its completion (proof lines 1032-1039).
Generators, continuity and openness of the induced map (proof lines 1039-1046).
Exactness under completion and the comparison of quotients (proof lines 1046-1053).
difficulty_reason: For a topological ring, a topological module over it, and a finitely generated ideal, the lemma asserts that if the module has an open submodule whose topology is I-adic then the completion has an open submodule whose topology is I-adic and the quotients of the completion by the powers of I agree with those of the module (statement lines 1024-1030). The proof chooses such an open submodule and notes that the powers of the ideal times it form a fundamental system of open submodules, so the completion of the module contains the completion of that submodule as an open submodule whose topology is I-adic by the corresponding algebra statement (proof lines 1032-1039). For the comparison of quotients it uses finite generation of the powers of the ideal: choosing generators gives a continuous open surjection from a finite direct sum onto the power of the ideal times the module, and the auxiliary exactness statement for short exact sequences under completion then shows that the same generators induce a surjection from the completion of the finite direct sum onto the kernel of the map from the completion to the quotient (proof lines 1039-1053). The claim is H2: the first half is a short transfer, and the second half requires a choice of generators and an application of the exactness criterion for completions, which is where finite generation is used.
